questions.q: If the sum of a certain number of terms of the A.P. $25,22,19, \ldots$ is 116 then the last term is
questions.solution:
$a=25, d=22-25=-3 \text {. }$
Let $n$ be the no. of terms
$\begin{array}{l}
\text { Sum }=116 ; \\
\text { Sum }=\frac{n}{2}[2 a+(n-1) d] \\
116=\frac{n}{2}[50+(n-1)(-3)] \\
\text { or }232=n[50-3 n+3]=n[53-3 n]=-3 n^{2}+53 n \\
\Rightarrow 3 n^{2}-53+232=0 \\
\Rightarrow(n-8)(3 n-29)=0 \\
\Rightarrow n=8 \text { or }}n=\frac{29}{3},$\\
n $\neq \frac{29}{3}$\\
\therefore n=8 \\
\therefore $\text { Now, } \mathrm{T}_{8}=$a+(8-1) d=25+7 $\times(-$3)=25-21=4 \\
\therefore $\text { Last term }=$4
\end{array}

questions.q:
The sum to $\mathrm{n}$ terms of the series
$\frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{4}+\frac{7}{8}+\frac{15}{16}+\ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{4}+\frac{7}{8}+\frac{15}{16}+\ldots \\=&\left(1-\frac{1}{2}\right)+\left(1-\frac{1}{4}\right)+\left(1-\frac{1}{8}\right)+\left(1-\frac{1}{16}\right)+\ldots . \\=& \mathrm{n}-\frac{\frac{1}{2}\left\{1-\frac{1}{2^{\mathrm{n}}}\right\}}{1-\frac{1}{2}}=\mathrm{n}-1+2^{-\mathrm{n}} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: If 64,27,36 are the Pth $Q$ th and $R$ th terms of a GP, then $P+2 Q$ is equal to
questions.solution: Let a be the first term and \(r\) be the common ration of a GP. \(\therefore P^{\text {th }}, Q^{\text {th }}\) and \(R^{\text {th }}\) terms of a GP are respectively ar \({ }^{\mathrm{P}-$1}\), ar \(\mathrmQ^{-1}\) and \({a r}^{\mathrm{R}-$1}\). According to question, \(a r^{P-1}=64 \ldots . .\) (i) \(a r^{Q-1}=27 \ldots . .\) (ii) \(a r^{R-1}=36 \ldots . .\) (iii) Dividing Eq. (i) by Eq. (ii), we get \(\mathrmr^{\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{Q}}=\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)^{3} \ldots \ldots$\) (iv) Dividing Eq. (ii) by Eq. (iii), we get \(\begin{array}{l} \mathrmr^{\mathrm{Q}-\mathrm{R}}=\frac{3}{4}\\ \Rightarrow \mathrmr^{3 $\mathrm{Q}-$3 $\mathrm{R}}=$\$left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^{3} \end{array}\) Multiplying Eq. (iv) and Eq. (v), we get \$(\begin{array}{l} \mathrmr^{\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{Q}}\times \mathrmr^{3 \mathrm{Q}-3 \mathrm{R}}=$1 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrmr^{\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{Q}+$3 $\mathrm{Q}-$3 $\mathrm{R}}=1 \\ \Rightarrow \mathrmr^{\mathrm{P}+$2 $\mathrm{Q}-$3 $\mathrm{R}}=\mathrmr^{0} \\ \Rightarrow $\mathrm{P}+$2 $\mathrm{Q}-$3 $\mathrm{R}=$0 \\ \Rightarrow $\mathrm{P}+$2 $\mathrm{Q}=$3 $\mathrm{R} \end{array}$\)

questions.q:
If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma \in[0, \pi]$ and if $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are in AP, then
$\frac{\sin \alpha-\sin \gamma}{\cos \gamma-\cos \alpha}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\frac{\sin \alpha-\sin \gamma}{\cos \gamma-\cos \alpha}=\frac{2 \cos \frac{\alpha+\gamma}{2} \sin \frac{\alpha-\gamma}{2}}{2 \sin \frac{\alpha+\gamma}{2} \cdot \sin \frac{\alpha-\gamma}{2}}$
$=\cot \frac{\alpha+\gamma}{2}$
\left[\begin{array}{l}\because \sin A-\sin B=2 \cos \left(\frac{A+B}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{A-B}{2}\right) \\ \text { and } \cos A-\cos B=2 \sin $\$left(\frac{A+B}{2}\right) \sin \left(\frac{B-A}{2}\right)\end{array}\right]
But $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are in $AP$
$\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{\alpha+\gamma}{2}=\beta
So, required value is $\cot \beta$.$

questions.q: Between the numbers& $2$~and~$20, 8$& means are inserted, then their sum is
questions.solution:
$2, {A}_{1}, {A}_{2}, \ldots {A}_{8}, 20$~are in~$A . P .$

where~${A}_{1}, {A}_{2}, \ldots {A}_{8}$~are~$8$~Arithmetic means between $2$ and $20$.

Using the property that the sum of all the means inserted between two numbers is equal to the product of the number of means and the AM of the first and last terms.

So,~${A}_{1} + {A}_{2} + . . . . + {A}_{8} = \left(\dfrac{2 + 20}{2}\right) \times 8 = 88$

questions.q: If the ${2}^{nd}, {5}^{th}$ and ${9}^{th}$ terms of a non-constant arithmetic progression are in geometric progression, then the common ratio of this geometric progression is
questions.solution:
Let the A.P. be $a, a + d, a + 2d, . . . . .$

Given, \left(a + d\right) . \left(a + 8d\right) = {\left(a + 4d\right)}^{2}$

$a^{2} + 9ad + 8d^{2} = a^{2} + 8ad + 16d^{2}$

$8d^{2} - ad = 0$

$d\left[8d - a\right] = 0$

$∵d \ne 0$

$d = \dfrac{a}{8}$

So, ${2}^{nd}$ term, ${5}^{th}$ term, ${9}^{th}$ term

would be \left(a + \dfrac{a}{8}\right)$, \left(a + \dfrac{a}{2}\right)$, \left(a + a\right)$

$\dfrac{9a}{8}$, $\dfrac{3a}{2}$, $2a$

Common Ratio $= \dfrac{{2}^{nd}term}{{1}^{st}term} = \dfrac{3a \times 8}{2 \times 9a} = \dfrac{4}{3}$

questions.q: Let $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ be the roots of the equation $x^{3} + 6x^{2} - px - 42 = 0 .$ If $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are in arithmetic progression then \left|\alpha\right| + \left|\beta\right| + \left|\gamma\right| =
questions.solution:
Let, $\alpha = \beta - d$ and $\gamma = \beta + d$
$\beta - d, \beta, \beta + d$ are the roots
$\beta - d + \beta + \beta + d = - 6 ⇒ \beta = - 2$
\left(\beta - d\right)\beta\left(\beta + d\right) = 42 ⇒ \left(- 2 - d\right)\left(- 2\right)\left(- 2 + d\right) = 42$
$⇒ \left(2 + d\right)2\left(2 - d\right) = - 42 ⇒ 4 - d^{2} = - 21$
$⇒ d^{2} = 25 ⇒ d = \pm 5$
$⇒$ The roots are $- 7, - 2,3$
$⇒ \left|\alpha\right| + \left|\beta\right| + \left|\gamma\right| = 12

questions.q: If $x, \left|x + 1\right|$ and \left|x - 1\right|$ are the first three terms of an arithmetic progression, then its sum upto $20$ terms is$
questions.solution:
$2\left|x + 1\right| = x + \left|x - 1\right|$
(i) Case- $Ι$ :-

$x \le - 1$
$2\left(- x - 1\right) = x + \left(- x + 1\right) ⇒ - 2x - 2 = 1$
$⇒ x = - \dfrac{3}{2}$
Then the A.P. is $\to - \dfrac{3}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{5}{2} . . . . . .$
${S}_{20} = \dfrac{20}{2}\left[- 3 + 19 \times 2\right] = \dfrac{20}{2} \times 35 = 350$
(ii) Case- $ΙΙ$ :-
$- 1 \le x < 1$
$2\left(x + 1\right) = x + \left(- x + 1\right) ⇒ 2x + 2 = 1 ⇒ x = - \dfrac{1}{2}$
Then the A.P. is $\to - \dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{3}{2} . . . . . .$
${S}_{20} = \dfrac{20}{2}\left[- 1 + 19 \times 1\right] = 10 \times 18 = 180$
(ii) Case- $ΙΙΙ$ :-
$x \ge 1$
$2\left(x + 1\right) = x + x - 1 ⇒ 2x + 2 = 2x - 1 ⇒ 2 = - 1$
(not possible)
Hence, the required sum is $350$ or $180$

questions.q: Let the sum of the first $n$ terms of a non-constant $A . P . , {a}_{1}, {a}_{2}, {a}_{3}, . . . . , {a}_{n}$ be $50n + \dfrac{n ( n - 7 )}{2}A,$ where $A$ is a constant. If $d$ is the common difference of this $A . P .$, then the ordered pair  \left(d, {a}_{50}\right)$ is equal to$
questions.solution:
Given sum of& $n$ terms is~${S}_{n} = 50n + \dfrac{n\left(n - 7\right)}{2}A \ldots ( 1 )$

$⇒ {S}_{n - 1} = 50 ( n - 1 ) + \dfrac{( n - 1 ) \left(n - 8\right)}{2}A \ldots \left($2\right)$

Subtracting~$( 1 )$ and $( 2 ) ,$~we get

${S}_{n} - {S}_{n - 1} = 50n - $50\left($n - 1\right) + $\dfrac{n\left(n - 7\right)}{2}$A - $\dfrac{\left(n - 1\right)\left(n - 8\right)}{2}$A$

$⇒ {S}_{n} - {S}_{n - 1} = 50 \left($n - n + 1\right) + $\dfrac{A}{2}\lleft(n \left(n - 7\right) - \left(n - 1\$right)\left($n - 8\right)\right)$

$⇒ {S}_{n} - {S}_{n - 1} = 50 + $\dfrac{A}{2} \left($n^{2} - 7n - n^{2} + 9n - 8\right)$

$⇒ {T}_{n} = {S}_{n} - {S}_{n - 1} = 50 + A ( n - 4 )$

Hence,~${T}_{1} = 50 - 3A$~and~${T}_{2} = 50 - 2A$

$⇒ d = {T}_{2} - {T}_{1} = A$~and~${T}_{50} = 50 + 46A .$

$
